correctness.rationale: PASS — For a C³ strictly convex oval with κ>0 and iid positive C¹ arclength density f, rooting three ordered samples just after their unique largest cyclic gap gives exactly a 6 ds da db density. In the only logarithmically dominant corner (a,b small), determinant and perimeter expansions uniformly yield r=κ(s)ab/4·(1+o(1)), even for unequal a,b. The sublevel cusp ab<4t/κ has area (4t/κ)t^0 log(1/t)+O(t), while one-small-gap boundary strips are O(t); hence P(r<t)~24t log(L/t)∫f³/κ. With v=log(a/L)/log(t/L), w=r/t, derivative r_b≈κ a/4 gives local jacobian 4t log(L/t)/κ and normalized density f³/(κ I); concentration, pointwise density and Scheffé justify total variation. Hölder yields unique f∝sqrt κ; Cauchy–Schwarz plus ∫κ ds=2π yields uniform-density circle minimum 12/(π L); layer cake gives p<1. Independent exact circle normalization confirms 24I=6/π² when L=2π, matching prior circle tail. No sampled experiment is used as an infinite proof.
